subject: Prosthodontics
title: Identify what a prosthesis replaces

units.title: Complete versus partial dentures
units.lesson: A complete denture replaces all teeth in an edentulous arch. A removable partial denture replaces some missing teeth while natural teeth remain. “Complete” and “partial” describe replacement extent; “removable” describes whether the prosthesis can be taken out. Keep these classification dimensions separate instead of treating every tooth replacement as the same design.
units.question: Which description fits a removable partial denture?
choices: Replaces some missing teeth while others remain
Always replaces every tooth in both arches
Restores only the colour of enamel
units.explanation: Partial refers to replacement of some, not all, teeth.
rationales: A denture replaces teeth, not merely colour.

units.title: Recognize a restorative crown
units.lesson: A restorative crown covers a tooth to restore form and function. Distinguish this manufactured restoration from the anatomical crown, the part of a natural tooth covered by enamel. A crown restoration is not synonymous with an implant root or an entire removable denture. This vocabulary exercise does not decide when a particular patient needs coverage.
units.question: Which statement correctly describes a restorative crown?
choices: It always replaces every tooth in an arch
It is a covering restoration for a tooth
It is identical to an implant root
units.explanation: A restorative crown covers a tooth; it differs from an entire denture or implant support.
rationales: An implant support is a different component.

units.title: Understand a fixed bridge
units.lesson: A fixed bridge replaces a missing tooth or teeth with a prosthesis retained by supporting structures. A conventional tooth-supported example links a replacement tooth to restorations on neighbouring teeth. The patient does not remove a fixed bridge for routine cleaning. This explains a design category, not a claim that every missing tooth should receive a bridge.
units.question: What does “fixed” indicate here?
choices: The patient routinely removes it like a removable denture
It is another word for natural enamel
It is retained in place rather than routinely removed by the patient

units.title: Separate implant from replacement tooth
units.lesson: A dental implant replaces a root-support role in the jaw and can support a crown, bridge or denture. The implant and the visible replacement tooth are not the same component. “Implant-supported” describes the support, while crown, bridge or denture describes the prosthesis. No placement technique or individual suitability decision is taught here.
units.question: Which statement separates implant and prosthesis?
choices: An implant can support a crown, bridge or denture
An implant is always a removable partial denture
An implant is natural enamel
units.explanation: The implant provides support for different prosthetic forms.
rationales: It is not always one prosthesis type.

units.title: Complete versus partial dentures · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: An edentulous arch has every tooth replaced by one prosthesis. Which classification describes replacement extent?
choices: Removable partial denture
Complete denture
Single-tooth crown
units.explanation: Complete replacement refers to all teeth in an edentulous arch.
rationales: Partial implies some natural teeth remain.
A single crown does not replace the whole arch.

units.title: Recognize a restorative crown · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an anatomical crown from a restorative crown?
choices: The former is part of the natural tooth; the latter is a manufactured covering
Both mean an implant root in the jaw
Both always mean a removable full-arch prosthesis
units.explanation: One term describes natural anatomy and the other a restoration.
rationales: An implant root is a different component.
Neither definition requires a removable full arch.

units.title: Understand a fixed bridge · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: A paper design links a replacement tooth to supporting restorations on neighbouring teeth. Which category fits?
choices: Conventional tooth-supported fixed bridge
Complete removable denture
Natural anatomical crown only
units.explanation: The described design is a conventional tooth-supported bridge.
rationales: The description does not replace an entire edentulous arch.
A natural crown is not a replacement assembly.

units.title: Separate implant from replacement tooth · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: Which pairing separates the support from the visible replacement in an implant-supported single-tooth restoration?
choices: Implant support and restorative crown
Anatomical enamel and primary tooth follicle
Complete denture and remaining natural teeth
units.explanation: The implant supplies support and the crown is the visible prosthetic restoration.
rationales: This is a different replacement context.
